messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] stepwiseqtl sensitive to max qtl settings
parts:
The LOD scores start to get a bit crazy when you fit models with a lot of QTL and interactions.

There are also some very tightly linked loci, which are probably artifacts.

karl

parts: Thank you for the quick response! I appreciate the information.

On Wednesday, December 23, 2015 at 11:30:35 PM UTC-5, Karl Broman wrote:
The LOD scores start to get a bit crazy when you fit models with a lot of QTL and interactions.

There are also some very tightly linked loci, which are probably artifacts.

karl


> On Dec 23, 2015, at 9:16 AM, sandr...@gmail.com wrote:
>
> Hello R/qtl community,
>
> I am mapping QTL using a doubled haploid plant population (N=149) with 1400 markers across 9 chromosomes. The optimal model identified using stepwiseqtl changes dependent upon the settings for max.qtl, also the LOD scores are dramatically different in the outputs:
>
> if max.qtl=15: 14QTL+8epistatic interactions with a maxLOD of 86
> if max.qtl=10: 10QTL+4interactions maxLOD of 32
> if max.qtl=5: 4QTL+1interaction maxLOD of 11
>
> What is the best approach for deciding the maximum # of QTL?
>
> Any advice would be greatly appreciated.
>
> Thank you,
> Sandra
>
> x<-sim.geno(x, n.draws=100, step=0.5, error.prob=0.01, map.function="kosambi")
> all_perms<-scantwo(x, pheno.col=pht,method="imp", model="normal", n.perm=1000)
>
> > print(pens<-calc.penalties(all_perms, alpha=.05))
>     main    heavy    light
> 2.807761 4.007467 1.902469
>
> step15<-stepwiseqtl(x, pheno.col=pht,method="imp", model="normal", max.qtl=15,penalties=pens,additive.only=FALSE, refine.locations=TRUE,keeptrace=TRUE, keeplodprofile=TRUE)
> step10<-stepwiseqtl(x, pheno.col=pht,method="imp", model="normal", max.qtl=10,penalties=pens,additive.only=FALSE, refine.locations=TRUE,keeptrace=TRUE, keeplodprofile=TRUE)
> step5<-stepwiseqtl(x, pheno.col=pht,method="imp", model="normal", max.qtl=5,penalties=pens,additive.only=FALSE, refine.locations=TRUE,keeptrace=TRUE, keeplodprofile=TRUE)
